question: According to the Illinois CDL manual, how far can the danger zone extend from the front bumper of a school bus?
choice_a: 10 feet
choice_c: 30 feet
explanation: The danger zones may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.1.1 Danger Zones

question: Why is the area to the left of a school bus always considered a danger zone, regardless of distance?
choice_a: Because the fuel tank is located there
choice_c: Because the driver cannot open a window there
choice_d: Because the stop arm blocks the driver's view there
explanation: The manual states the area to the left of the bus is always considered dangerous because of passing cars.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.1.1 Danger Zones

question: When properly adjusted, the outside left and right side flat mirrors should let the driver see approximately how far behind the bus?
choice_a: 50 feet or one bus length
choice_c: 200 feet or four bus lengths
explanation: Flat mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet or four bus lengths behind the bus.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.1.3 Outside Left and Right Side Flat Mirrors

question: According to the manual, when should more students be killed relative to bus riding: while getting on/off the bus, or while riding as passengers inside?
choice_a: More students are killed while riding inside the bus each year
choice_b: More students are killed getting on or off a school bus each year than as passengers inside
choice_c: Fatalities are approximately equal between the two situations
choice_d: The manual states no students are ever killed while loading or unloading
explanation: The manual states more students are killed while getting on or off a school bus each year than are killed as passengers inside a school bus.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.2 Loading and Unloading

question: When approaching a school bus stop, if equipped, the alternating flashing amber warning lights should be activated at least how far (or how many seconds) before the stop, per the general guidance given (outside an urban area)?
choice_a: 50 feet or one to two seconds
choice_b: 100 feet, or approximately three to five seconds
choice_c: 200 feet (100 in an urban area), or approximately five to 10 seconds
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to activate alternating flashing amber warning lights at least 200 feet (100 feet in an urban area) or approximately five to 10 seconds before the school bus stop, or in accordance with state law.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: When stopping to load students, the front bumper of the bus should come to a full stop how far from the students at the designated stop?
choice_a: At least 5 feet
choice_c: At least 20 feet
explanation: The bus should stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students, forcing them to walk to the bus so the driver has a better view of their movements.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.2.1 Approaching the Stop

question: If the driver has missed a student's unloading stop, what does the manual instruct?
choice_a: Back up immediately to the correct stop
choice_b: Do not back up; follow local procedures
choice_c: Call the parents before continuing the route
choice_d: Continue the route and report it only at the end of the day
explanation: The manual notes: if you have missed a student's unloading stop, do not back up, and be sure to follow local procedures.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.2.3 Unloading Procedures on the Route

question: When a student must cross the roadway after exiting the bus, where should they stop and wait for the driver's signal?
choice_a: At least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper, at the right edge of the roadway
choice_c: At the rear bumper of the bus
choice_d: In the middle of the roadway
explanation: Students should walk to a location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper and stop at the right edge of the roadway, where the driver can see their feet, before waiting for a signal to cross.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.2.3 Additional Procedures for Students Who Must Cross the Roadway

question: During a post-trip inspection, what should the driver look for while walking through and around the bus?
choice_a: Only fuel level and tire pressure
choice_b: Articles left, sleeping students, open windows and doors, mechanical/operational problems, and damage or vandalism
choice_c: Only the ABS malfunction lamp
explanation: The post-trip inspection includes checking for articles left on the bus, sleeping students, open windows and doors, mechanical/operational problems (including mirror systems, warning lamps, and stop signal arms), and damage or vandalism.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.2.6 Post-trip Inspection

question: As a general rule, is it better to keep students on the bus during an emergency or evacuate them immediately?
choice_a: Always evacuate immediately in any emergency
choice_b: Student safety and control are best maintained by keeping students on the bus, unless doing so exposes them to unnecessary risk or injury
choice_c: Evacuation should only happen if a supervisor orders it by radio
choice_d: Students should be evacuated only after the bus has been towed
explanation: The manual states that as a general rule, student safety and control are best maintained by keeping students on the bus during an emergency, if doing so does not expose them to unnecessary risk or injury.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.3.1 Planning for Emergencies

question: Which of the following is listed as a condition under which the driver MUST evacuate the bus?
choice_a: The bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing
choice_b: The bus air conditioning has stopped working
choice_c: A student has a minor cut
choice_d: The bus is running five minutes late
explanation: Mandatory evacuation conditions include the bus being on fire or threatened by fire, stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing, in a position that may change and increase danger, in imminent danger of collision, or facing a hazardous materials spill.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.3.1 Mandatory Evacuations

question: According to the manual's tips for determining a safe place after evacuation, how far off the road (in the direction of oncoming traffic) should a safe place generally be?
choice_a: At least 25 feet
choice_c: At least 100 feet
explanation: A safe place will be at least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic, to keep students from being hit by debris if another vehicle collides with the bus.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: If there is risk from a spilled hazardous material, how far upwind of the bus should students be led during evacuation?
choice_a: At least 50 feet
choice_c: At least 200 feet
explanation: The manual instructs leading students upwind of the bus at least 300 feet if there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.3.2 Evacuation Procedures

question: What distinguishes a passive railroad-highway crossing from an active crossing?
choice_a: A passive crossing has flashing red lights and gates, while an active crossing has none
choice_b: A passive crossing has no traffic control device, while an active crossing has devices such as flashing lights or gates
choice_c: A passive crossing is only found on multi-lane highways
choice_d: A passive crossing requires no stop, while an active crossing always requires a stop
explanation: Passive crossings have no traffic control device installed, requiring the driver to decide whether it is safe to cross, while active crossings have devices like flashing red lights and gates to regulate traffic.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.4.1 Types of Crossings

question: When approaching a railroad-highway crossing, at approximately what distance should a school bus driver activate hazard lights?
choice_a: Approximately 50 feet before the crossing
choice_c: Approximately 200 feet before the crossing
explanation: The manual instructs activating hazard lights approximately 200 feet before the crossing to make sure your intentions are known.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures

question: At a railroad-highway crossing, where you have the best view of the tracks, how close and how far should you stop from the nearest rail?
choice_a: No closer than 5 feet and no farther than 20 feet
choice_b: No closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet
choice_c: No closer than 25 feet and no farther than 75 feet
choice_d: No closer than 50 feet and no farther than 100 feet
explanation: Drivers should stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, where they have the best view of the tracks.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.4.3 Recommended Procedures / Illinois School Bus Safety Information

question: As a general rule for containment or storage area beyond a railroad crossing, how many feet should be added to the length of the school bus?
choice_a: 5 feet
choice_c: 15 feet
explanation: As a general rule, drivers should add 15 feet to the length of the school bus to determine an acceptable amount of containment or storage area on the far side of a crossing.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.4.4 Special Situations, Containment or Storage Areas

question: Under the Department of Transportation requirement cited in the manual, air brake vehicles built on or after what date must have antilock braking systems (ABS)?
choice_a: January 1, 1995
choice_c: June 1, 2000
explanation: The DOT requires ABS on air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers and converter dollies) built on or after March 1, 1999.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.6.1 Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: In emergency braking on a school bus equipped with ABS, what should the driver avoid doing?
choice_a: Applying steady brake pressure
choice_c: Steering around obstacles
explanation: The manual states that in emergency braking, drivers should not pump the brakes on a bus equipped with ABS.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.6.3 Braking with ABS

question: What is the maximum tail swing a school bus can have, according to the manual?
choice_a: 1 foot
choice_c: 3 feet
explanation: A school bus can have up to a 3-foot tail swing, so drivers need to check mirrors before and during any turning movements.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.7.4 Tail Swing

question: According to the manual, backing a school bus should never be done under which circumstance?
choice_a: When students are outside of the bus
choice_c: When the parking brake is set
explanation: Backing is strongly discouraged and should never be done when students are outside of the bus, as it increases the risk of a collision.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, 10.7.3 Backing

question: To obtain the School Bus (S) endorsement, which knowledge tests must a driver first pass, based on Sections 2 and 4 of the manual?
choice_a: The Hazmat and Tanker tests
choice_b: The General (core) Knowledge and Passenger endorsement tests
choice_c: Only the air brakes test
explanation: To obtain the S endorsement, drivers must first pass the general (core) knowledge and Passenger endorsement tests based on Sections 2 and 4 of the manual, plus the air brakes test if the bus has air brakes.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, How to obtain the School Bus Endorsement (S) and Illinois SBP

question: What is the minimum age requirement for an Illinois School Bus Permit (SBP) applicant/driver?
choice_a: 18 years old
choice_c: 21 years old
explanation: An SBP applicant/driver must be age 21 or older.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, How to obtain the School Bus Endorsement (S) and Illinois SBP

question: Which Illinois Secretary of State office can be contacted for questions about the Illinois school bus permit program, and what is its phone number?
choice_a: The Safe Ride section, 217-782-7674
choice_c: The Commercial Licensing Unit, 217-524-2600
explanation: Applicants or drivers with questions about the Illinois school bus permit program can contact the Illinois Secretary of State's Safe Ride section at 217-782-7674.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, How to obtain the School Bus Endorsement (S) and Illinois SBP

question: Per the Illinois-specific safety information, no child may cross a highway under which condition?
choice_a: A two-lane highway with no center markings
choice_b: A highway with four or more lanes where at least one or more lanes travel in the opposite direction
choice_c: Any highway posted at 35 mph or less
choice_d: A highway with a marked crosswalk
explanation: No child may cross any highway with four or more lanes of traffic where at least one or more lanes travel in the opposite direction; the bus stop must instead be situated so the student's residence and/or school is on the right side of the highway.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, Illinois School Bus Safety Information

question: Under Illinois school bus safety rules, the amber lights of the eight-lamp flashing signal system must be activated at least how far before a stop outside an urban area?
choice_a: 50 feet
choice_c: 200 feet
explanation: The amber lights of the eight-lamp flashing signal system must be activated when approaching a stop at least 100 feet within an urban area, or 200 feet outside an urban area.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 10.M, Illinois School Bus Safety Information, Get Them There Safely

question: What is unique about the Charter Bus (C) endorsement compared to other CDL endorsements described in the manual?
choice_a: It is a federally mandated endorsement required in all states
choice_c: It replaces the Passenger (P) endorsement entirely
choice_d: It is only available to drivers under age 21
explanation: The manual states the Charter Bus (C) endorsement is an Illinois only endorsement.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 11, General Information

question: Who is required to apply for a Charter Bus (C) endorsement?
choice_a: Any person who drives a school bus on a regular route
choice_b: Any person who drives a bus, other than a school bus, chartered by a school solely to transport students in 12th grade and under to or from a school-sponsored activity
choice_c: Any person who drives a charter bus for corporate events
choice_d: Any person who drives a passenger vehicle for hire
explanation: The C endorsement applies to a person who drives a bus, other than a school bus, chartered by a school for the sole purpose of transporting students in 12th grade and under to or from any school-sponsored activity.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 11, General Information

question: Under what circumstance is the Charter Bus (C) endorsement NOT required for a driver operating a chartered bus for school children?
choice_a: If the driver already possesses a CDL with Passenger (P) and School Bus (S) endorsements, along with an Illinois SBP of the same class as the charter bus
choice_b: If the driver has more than five years of experience
choice_c: If the trip is under 50 miles
choice_d: If the bus has fewer than 16 seats
explanation: The Charter Bus endorsement is not required if the driver already possesses a CDL with Passenger (P) and School Bus (S) endorsements, along with an Illinois SBP of the same class as the charter bus he or she will be operating.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 11, General Information

question: If a driver already holds the proper class CDL with at least a Passenger (P) endorsement, what is required to obtain the Charter Bus (C) endorsement?
choice_a: Only the charter bus knowledge test, after submitting a CB1 form
choice_b: The full General Knowledge, Passenger, and Air Brakes tests again
choice_c: A new road test only, with no written test
explanation: A driver who already holds the proper class CDL with at least a P endorsement need only pass the charter bus knowledge test, after submitting a Charter Bus endorsement form (CB1) obtained from a registered bus company.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 11, Testing Information

question: What is the minimum age requirement to obtain a Charter Bus endorsement in Illinois?
choice_a: 18 years old
choice_c: 21 years old
explanation: Among the driver requirements, an applicant for the Charter Bus endorsement must be age 21 or older.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 11, Driver Requirements

question: Besides age and a valid classified license, which of the following is a listed requirement to obtain a Charter Bus endorsement?
choice_a: Submit to and pass an Illinois-specific criminal background check through an approved vendor
choice_b: Own the charter bus vehicle personally
choice_c: Have at least 10 years of commercial driving experience
choice_d: Complete a college degree in transportation
explanation: Driver requirements for the Charter Bus endorsement include submitting to and successfully passing an Illinois specific criminal background check through an approved vendor, as well as a medical exam including drug testing.
source_note: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Guide (July 2025 edition, DSD CDL 10.30), Illinois Secretary of State -- Section 11, Driver Requirements
